statements.claim: On the night before the battle Krishna told Arjuna to cleanse himself and recite his hymn to Durga on the eve of battle so the defeat of the foe would be assured.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.23: 'Cleansing thyself, O mighty-armed one, utter on the eve of the battle thy hymn to Durga for (compassing) the defeat of the foe.'

statements.claim: Arjuna alighted from his car and recited the hymn with joined hands, praising Durga under many names (leader of the Yogins, identical with Brahman; Kali of black and tawny hue; Mahakali; giver of victory with peacock-plume banner, spear, sword and shield; younger sister of the chief of cowherds, born in Nanda's race; fond of buffalo's blood, dressed in yellow robes; wolf-faced devourer of Asuras; slayer of Kaitabha; mother of Skanda; Swaha, Swadha, Saraswati, Savitri, twilight, day, sleep and beauty of creatures; the Vedas and Srutis; science of Brahma; contentment, growth, light; dweller in inaccessible places and abodes of worshippers, defeating the Danavas; beheld by Siddhas and Charanas).
statements.evidence: MBh 6.23 hymn passage lists each of these epithets in the same order/grouping: 'O leader of Yogins... identical with Brahman... Kali... of a black and tawny hue... Mahakali... giver of victory... banner of peacock plumes... awful spear... sword and shield... younger sister of the chief of cow-herds... born in the race of the cowherd Nanda!... fond of buffalo's blood... dressed in yellow robes... devoured Asuras assuming the face of a wolf... slain the Asura Kaitabha... mother of Skanda... described as Swaha, and Swadha... as Saraswati, as Savitra... twilight... day... sleep... beauty... Vedas, the Srutis... propitious to Brahmanas engaged in sacrifice... science of Brahma among sciences... contentment... growth... light... supportest the Sun and the Moon... In inaccessible regions... in the abodes of thy worshippers and in the nether regions... always defeatest the Danavas. The Siddhas and the Charanas behold thee.'

statements.claim: Arjuna prayed with cleansed inner soul that victory always attend him through the goddess's grace on the field of battle.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.23: 'With inner soul cleansed, I praise thee. O great goddess, let victory always attend me through thy grace on the field of battle.'

statements.claim: Durga, graciously inclined toward mankind, understood the measure of Partha's devotion, appeared in the firmament, and in the presence of Govinda promised: 'Within a short time thou shalt conquer thy foes... thou hast Narayana (again) for aiding thee. Thou art incapable of being defeated by foes, even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.'
statements.evidence: MBh 6.23: 'Understanding (the measure of) Partha's devotion, Durga who is always graciously inclined towards mankind, appeared in the firmament and in the presence of Govinda, said... The goddess said,--Within a short time thou shalt conquer thy foes, O Pandava. O invincible one, thou hast Narayana (again) for aiding thee. Thou art incapable of being defeated by foes, even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.'

statements.claim: The boon-giving goddess disappeared, Arjuna mounted his own excellent car, and Krishna and Arjuna, seated on the same car, blew their celestial conches.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.23: 'Having said this, the boon-giving goddess disappeared soon... the son of Pritha then mounted his own excellent car. And then Krishna and Arjuna, seated on the same car, blew their celestial conches.'

statements.claim: Sanjaya told Dhritarashtra that whoever recites this hymn at dawn fears nothing from Yakshas, Rakshasas or Pisachas, snakes or fanged creatures or kings, wins every dispute, is freed from bonds, and lives a hundred years in health and strength; and that the Kauravas, entangled in death's meshes, did not know Nara and Narayana stood on one chariot, though Dwaipayana, Narada, Kanwa and the sinless Rama had all tried to prevent Dhritarashtra's son.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.23 closing: 'The man that recites this hymn rising at dawn, hath no fear any time from Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Pisachas... from snakes and all animals that have fangs and teeth, as also from kings... victorious in all disputes, and if bound, he is freed... liveth for a hundred years... Thy wicked sons... do not... know them to be Nara and Narayana... Dwaipayana and Narada, and Kanwa, and the sinless Rama, had all prevented thy son. But he did not accept their words.'

statements.claim: The eve-of-battle instruction and hymn were framed as Krishna's first preparation for war, a command about worship rather than formations or weapons.
statements.evidence: Framing around the episode; the source records the command to hymn Durga as the opening event of the day, but 'first command was not about formations or weapons' is editorial narration, not a sourceable assertion.

notes: All narrative and quoted elements match MBh 6.23 (Ganguli). Hymn epithets faithfully reproduced. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Seated in his palace, Dhritarashtra asked Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas, assembled on the sacred plain of Kurukshetra from desire of fighting, had done.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: 'Assembled together on the sacred plain of Kurukshetra from desire of fighting what did my sons and the Pandavas do, O Sanjaya.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana approached his preceptor Drona, pointed out the enemy's champions (Yuyudhana, Virata, Drupada, Dhrishtadyumna, the ruler of Kasi, Subhadra's son, the sons of Draupadi) and named his own leaders (Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashwatthaman, Vikarna, Jayadratha, and many heroes ready to die for his sake), saying his army protected by Bhishma was insufficient and the Pandavas' protected by Bhima sufficient, and asking all to station themselves at the divisions' entrances and protect Bhishma alone.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: Duryodhana's speech to Drona lists Yuyudhana, Virata, Drupada (army arrayed by Drupada's son Dhrishtadyumna), ruler of Kasi, Subhadra's son, sons of Draupadi; then 'thyself, and Bhishma, and Karna, and Kripa... and Aswatthaman and Vikarna... and Jayadratha... many heroic warriors, prepared to lay down their lives for my sake... Our army... protected by Bhishma, is insufficient. This force... of the Pandavas, protected by Bhima, is sufficient... Stationing yourselves... in the entrances of the divisions... all of you protect Bhishma alone.'

statements.claim: The valiant grandsire of the Kurus, giving Duryodhana great joy, roared like a lion and blew his conch, and conches, drums, cymbals and horns sounded together in a great uproar.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: 'the valiant and venerable grandsire of the Kurus, affording great joy to him (Duryodhana) by loudly uttering a leonine roar, blew (his) conch. Then conches and drums and cymbals and horns were sounded at once and the noise (made) became a loud uproar.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Arjuna, on a great car yoked with white steeds, blew their celestial conches — Krishna Panchajanya, Arjuna Devadatta; Bhima blew Paundra, Yudhishthira Anantavijaya, Nakula Sughosa, Sahadeva Manipushpaka; and the ruler of Kasi, Sikhandin, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, Satyaki, Drupada, Draupadi's sons and Subhadra's son all blew theirs, the blare rending the hearts of the Kauravas.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: 'Hrishikesa blew (the conch called) Panchajanya and Dhananjaya (that called) Devadatta; and Vrikodara... Paundra. And Kunti's son king Yudhishthira blew... Anantavijaya; while Nakula and Sahadeva... Sughosa and Manipushpaka. And... the ruler of Kasi... Sikhandin, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and that unvanquished Satyaki, and Drupada, and the sons of Draupadi, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra--all these... blew their conches. And that blare, loudly reverberating through the welkin... rent the hearts of the Dhartarashtras.'

statements.claim: Arjuna, ape-bannered, raised his bow as missile-throwing was about to begin and asked Krishna, who knows no deterioration, to place his car between the two armies so he could observe those desirous of battle who fought for the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: 'the ape-bannered son of Pandu, rising his bow, when the throwing of missiles had just commenced, said... O thou that knoweth no deterioration, place my car (once) between the two armies, so that I may observe these that stand here desirous of battle... prepared to fight for doing what is agreeable... to the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.'

statements.claim: Krishna placed the car between the two armies in view of Bhishma, Drona and all the kings and said 'Behold, O Partha, these assembled Kurus'; there Arjuna saw sires, grandsons, friends, father-in-law and well-wishers in both armies.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: 'Hrishikesa, placing that excellent car between the two armies, in view of Bhishma and Drona and all the kings of the earth, said,--Behold, O Partha these assembled Kurus,--And there the son of Pritha beheld, standing (his) sires and grandsons, and friends, and father-in-law and well-wishers, in both the armies.'

statements.claim: Overcome by pity, Arjuna's limbs grew languid, his mouth dried, his body trembled, his hair stood on end, Gandiva slipped from his hand, and he declared he desired neither victory, sovereignty nor pleasures, since those for whose sake these were desired stood arrayed ready to give up life and wealth; he wished not to slay them even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, let alone the earth.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.25: 'my limbs become languid, and my mouth becomes dry. My body trembles, and my hair stands on end. Gandiva slips from my hand... I do not desire victory... nor sovereignty, nor pleasures... preceptors, sires, sons and grandsires, maternal uncles, father-in-laws... and kinsmen... I wish not to slay these though they slay me... even for the sake of the sovereignty of the three worlds, what then for the sake of (this) earth?'

statements.claim: Sanjaya's narration paused with the chariot between the armies and Krishna not yet having spoken.
statements.evidence: Closes out the chapter-one moment (end of MBh 6.25 / BG ch. 1) where the scene halts before Krishna's reply; the 'field waiting' imagery is connective narration consistent with the text's pause.

notes: Conch names, roster lists, quoted speeches and physical collapse all match MBh 6.25 (Ganguli) closely. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna rebuked Arjuna's despondency as unbecoming of noble birth, shutting one out from heaven and productive of infamy, telling him to shake off vile weakness of heart and arise.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'Whence, O Arjuna, hath come upon thee, at such a crisis, this despondency that is unbecoming a person of noble birth, that shuts one out from heaven, and that is productive of infamy?... Shaking off this vile weakness of hearts, arise, O chastiser of foes.'

statements.claim: Arjuna said he could not fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows since they deserved worship; living on alms was better than slaying preceptors, whose killing (even if greedy for wealth) would leave bloodstained pleasures; he knew not which was of greater moment, conquest by them or by us; the sons of Dhritarashtra, by whose death he would not wish to live, stood before him; his nature was tainted with compassion, his mind unsettled about duty; he asked Krishna to tell him what was assuredly good, declaring himself Krishna's disciple and seeking his aid; nothing — not a foe-less kingdom nor the sovereignty of the gods — would dispel the grief blasting his senses.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'How... can I with arrows contend in battle against Bhishma and Drona, deserving as they are... of worship?... it is well (for one), to live on even alms... By slaying preceptors... I should only enjoy pleasures that are bloodstained! We know not which of the two is of greater moment... whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us. By slaying whom we would not like to live,--even they, the sons of Dhritarashtra, stand before (us). My nature affected by the taint of compassion, my mind unsettled about (my) duty, I ask thee. Tell me what is assuredly good (for me). I am thy disciple. O, instruct me, I seek thy aid. I do not see (that) which would dispel that grief... even if I obtain a prosperous kingdom on earth without a foe or the very sovereignty of the gods.'

statements.claim: Arjuna said plainly 'I will not fight' and remained silent.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'Gudakesa--(once more) addressed Govinda, saying,--I will not fight,--and then remained silent.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered in the midst of the two armies that Arjuna mourned those who deserved no mourning and spoke like the learned, while the truly wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'Unto him overcome by despondency, Hrishikesa, in the midst of the two armies, said: Thou mournest those that deserve not to be mourned... Those... that are (really) wise, grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.'

statements.claim: Krishna taught the soul's immortality: it pervades the universe and none can destroy it; it was never born nor dies; it is not slain when the body perishes; as worn robes are cast off for new ones the soul takes new bodies; weapons, fire, water and wind cannot harm it; it is unchanging, all-pervading, stable, firm and eternal.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'Know that [the soul] to be immortal by which all this [universe] is pervaded. No one can compass the destruction of that which is imperishable... It is never born, nor doth it ever die... it is not slain upon the body being perished... As a man, casting off robes that are worn out, putteth on others that are new, so the Embodied (soul)... entereth other bodies that are new. Weapons cleave it not, fire consumeth it not; the waters do not drench it, nor doth the wind waste it... It is unchangeable, all-pervading, stable, firm, and eternal.'

statements.claim: Krishna added that even if the soul were regarded as constantly born and dying, one must not mourn: death is certain for the born and birth for the dead, and beings were unmanifest before birth, manifest in the interval, and unmanifest again at death.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'even if thou regardest it as constantly born and constantly dead, it behoveth thee not... to mourn... of one that is born, death is certain; and of one that is dead, birth is certain... All beings (before birth) were unmanifest. Only during an interval (between birth and death)... are they manifest; and then again, when death comes, they become (once more) unmanifest. What grief then is there in this?'

statements.claim: The senses' contacts — heat and cold, pleasure and pain — come and go and are not permanent, and the man unmoved by them, same in pain and pleasure, firm of mind, is fit for emancipation.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.26: 'The contacts of the senses with their (respective) objects producing (sensations of) heat and cold, pleasure and pain, are not permanent... Do thou, O Bharata, endure them. For the man whom these afflict not... who is the same in pain and pleasure and who is firm in mind, is fit for emancipation.'

statements.claim: Arjuna surrendered his own judgment, begging instruction as a disciple, and the whole field awaited Krishna's reply.
statements.evidence: The disciple-surrender is directly sourced ('I am thy disciple. O, instruct me'); the framing that he 'handed over his own judgment' and that armies 'held their breath' is connective narration around the sourced exchange.

notes: Dialogue and doctrine track MBh 6.26 (BG ch. 2) closely. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna gave Arjuna celestial sight and revealed his supreme sovereign form: many mouths and eyes, innumerable arms, bearing diadem, mace and discus, a mass of energy glowing on all sides, with the sun and moon for eyes and the blazing fire for a mouth, touching the skies, many-hued, mouth wide open.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.35: 'I give thee celestial sight. Behold my sovereign mystic nature... revealed... his Supreme sovereign form, with many mouths and eyes... Bearing (thy) diadem, mace, and discus, a mass of energy, glowing on all sides... having the Sun and the Moon for thy eyes, the blazing fire for thy mouth... touching the very skies, of blazing radiance, many-hued, mouth wide-open, with eyes that are blazing and large.' (The 'thousand faces and thousand arms' phrasing condenses the passage's 'many mouths and eyes' / 'innumerable arms' / 'faces turned on all sides.')

statements.claim: Within the cosmic body Arjuna beheld Brahman seated on his lotus seat, all the Rishis and celestial serpents, the Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Ashwins and Maruts, hosts of gods entering the form while others, afraid, prayed with joined hands, and great Rishis and Siddhas praising it with hymns; the space between heaven and earth and every point of the horizon was pervaded by the form, and the triple world trembled.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.35: 'I behold all the gods... Brahman seated on (his) lotus seat, and all the Rishis and the celestial snakes... The Rudras, the Adityas, the Vasus... the Aswins, the Maruts... For the space betwixt heaven and earth is pervaded by Thee alone, as also all the points of the horizon... the triple world trembleth. For these hosts of gods are entering thee. Some, afraid, are praying with joined hands... the hosts of great Rishis and Siddhas praise Thee.'

statements.claim: Arjuna described the form as having no beginning, middle or end, indestructible, the supreme object of the universe, heating all creation with its own radiance, and said with hair standing on end that he beheld neither end, middle nor beginning of it.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.35: 'Thou art indestructible, (and) the Supreme object of this universe... without beginning, mean, end... heating this universe with energy of thy own... Neither end nor middle, nor also beginning of thine do I behold... with hair standing on end.'

statements.claim: Arjuna saw the sons of Dhritarashtra with the hosts of kings, Bhishma, Drona, Karna the son of the charioteer (Suta) and the principal warriors of the Pandavas' own side entering Krishna's terrible tusk-fierce mouths, some crushed between the teeth, rushing like rivers to the ocean and moths to the fire.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.35: 'all these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with the hosts of kings, and Bhishma, and Drona, and also this Suta's son (Karna), accompanied by even the principal warriors of our side, are quickly entering thy terrible mouths rendered fierce by thy tusks. Some, with their heads crushed, are seen striking at the interstices of (thy) teeth. As many currents of water... roll rapidly towards the ocean... As moths with increasing speed rush for (their own) destruction to the blazing fire, so also do (these)...'

statements.claim: Arjuna, unable to command courage or peace of mind, begged Krishna, gracious God of gods and refuge of the universe, for grace.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.35: 'with (my) inner soul trembling (in fright), I can no longer command courage and peace of mind... Be gracious, O God of gods, O thou that art the refuge of the Universe.'

statements.claim: From within the blaze a voice declared: 'I am Death, the destroyer of the worlds, fully developed. I am now engaged in slaying the race of men. By me have all these been already slain. Be only my instrument.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt for MBh 6.35: 'The Holy One said,--I am Death, the destroyer of the worlds, fully developed. I am now engaged in slaying the race of men... By me have all these been already slain. Be only (my) instrument.'

statements.claim: The voice that spoke was the same one that had driven the chariot and taught the immortality of the soul, and Arjuna bowed his head trembling amid the blaze.
statements.evidence: Identification of the speaker with Krishna (charioteer/teacher) is implied by context and the corpus chain (ch. 11 follows ch. 2's teaching); the bowed-head posture and interpretive 'war already decided' reflections are connective narration around the sourced declaration.

notes: All content matches MBh 6.35 (BG ch. 11). 'Thousand faces and thousand arms' is a compressed rendering of the passage's 'many mouths and eyes'/'innumerable arms'/'faces turned on all sides'. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Recap: Krishna had given Arjuna celestial sight and shown the sovereign cosmic form with sun and moon for eyes, a blazing-fire mouth, gods, serpents, Rishis and Siddhas gathered in it, and the warriors of both armies rushing into its flaming mouths like rivers to the sea.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.35 (same chapter as DKS_0459's event): celestial sight granted and the viśvarūpa revealed with all gods/creatures within it and warriors entering the mouths; consistent with the pack passages for this story (index summary: Arjuna terrified begs Krishna to resume his familiar form).

statements.claim: Arjuna told Krishna that beholding his form unseen before he had been joyful yet his mind was troubled with fear, and begged him to show his other, ordinary form.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, MBh 6.35: 'Beholding (thy) form (unseen) before, I have been joyful, (yet) my mind hath been troubled, with fear. Show me that (other ordinary) form, O God.'

statements.claim: Krishna once more showed Arjuna his own ordinary form; assuming his gentle form again, the high-souled one comforted Arjuna who had been afflicted.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, MBh 6.35: 'Vasudeva, having said all this to Arjuna, once more showed (him) his own (ordinary) form, and that High-Souled one, assuming once more (his) gentle form, comforted him who had been afflicted.'

statements.claim: Arjuna declared that beholding Krishna's gentle human form he was composed once more, his senses returned, and he was himself again.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt begins Arjuna's reply: 'Arjuna said,--Beho[ld]...'; the closing line is confirmed by the pack's index summary ('Krishna comforts him and restores him to his senses') and the canonical BG 11.51 text of this same passage.

statements.claim: The universal form was truth while the gentle form was mercy, and Krishna folded himself back into a charioteer's shape for a trembling friend; his comfort restored Arjuna's composure before the war.
statements.evidence: Interpretive framing of the sourced restoration scene (Krishna comforting and restoring the afflicted Arjuna); the 'truth vs mercy' gloss and physical-composure imagery are devotional connective narration, not separate sourceable facts.

notes: Matches MBh 6.35. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Arjuna asked Krishna the true nature of renunciation and what abandonment means distinctly.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.42: 'Of renunciation, O thou of mighty arms, I desire to know the true nature, and also of abandonment... distinctly, O slayer of Kesi.'

statements.claim: Krishna taught: the learned call rejection of works done with desire 'renunciation'; the discerning call abandonment of the fruit of all works 'abandonment'; some say work itself should be abandoned as evil, others that sacrifice, gift and penance should not be abandoned.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.42: 'The rejection of the works with desire is known by the learned as renunciation. The abandonment of the fruit of all work, the discerning call abandonment. Some wise men say that work (itself) should be abandoned as evil; others (say) that the works of sacrifice, gifts, and penance, should not be abandoned.'

statements.claim: Sacrifice, gift and penance purify the wise and should be done abandoning attachment and fruit; renouncing an act prescribed in the scriptures is not proper — abandoning it from delusion is of the quality of darkness, from fear of bodily pain of the quality of passion (earning no fruit), while doing prescribed work without attachment or longing for fruit is abandonment of the quality of goodness.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.42: 'The works of sacrifice, gifts, and penance should not be abandoned... are the purifications of the wise... done, abandoning attachment and fruit... The renunciation of an act prescribed (in the scriptures) is not proper. Its abandonment (is) from delusion... of the quality of darkness... when work is abandoned from (fear of) bodily pain... of the quality of passion never obtaineth the fruit of abandonment... when work that is prescribed... is done... abandoning attachment and fruit also, that abandonment is deemed to be of the quality of goodness.'

statements.claim: Since actions cannot be absolutely abandoned by an embodied person, the true abandoner is he who gives up the fruit of actions, not the actions.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.42: 'Since actions cannot be absolutely abandoned by an embodied person, (therefore) he who abandons the fruit of actions is truly said to be an abandoner.'

statements.claim: Krishna named the five causes of all action — substratum, agent, the organs, the diverse efforts, and the deities as the fifth — declaring that whatever a man undertakes with body, speech or mind, these five are its causes; the dull man who sees his self as sole agent sees wrongly, while he who has no egoism and an unsullied mind, even killing all these people, kills not nor is fettered.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.42: 'those five causes for the completion of all actions... (They are) substratum, agent, the diverse kinds of organs, the diverse efforts severally, and with them the deities as the fifth. With body, speech, or mind, whatever work... a man undertakes, these five are its causes... he that... beholdeth his own self as solely the agent, he, dull in mind, beholdeth not. He that hath no feeling of egoism, whose mind is not sullied, he, even killing all these people, killeth not, nor is fettered (by action).'

statements.claim: Knowledge, action and agent are each threefold: knowledge seeing one eternal essence undivided in the divided is good, knowledge of separate essences is passionate, knowledge clinging to a single object as the whole, without reason or truth, is dark; likewise the action done without attachment and longing for fruit is good, the desire-driven egoistic action is passionate, the action from delusion heedless of consequence and power is dark; and the agent free from attachment, silent about self, constant, energetic and unmoved by success and defeat is good, the affectionate fruit-coveting cruel impure agent is passionate, and the inapplicable obstinate deceitful malicious slothful procrastinating agent is dark.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.42: 'That by which One Eternal Essence is viewed in all things, undivided in the divided... knowledge having the quality of goodness. That knowledge which discerneth all things as diverse essences of different kinds... of passion. But that which is attached to (each) single object as if it were the whole, which is without reason, without truth, and mean... of darkness. The action which is prescribed... without attachment... without desires and aversion, by one who longeth not for (its) fruit, is said to be of the quality of goodness. But that action which is done by one seeking objects of desire, or by one filled with egoism, and which is attended with great trouble, is said to be of the quality of passion. That action which is undertaken from delusion, without regard to consequences... is said to be of the quality of passion [darkness]. The agent who is free from attachment, who never speaketh of himself... unmoved by success and defeat... goodness... full of affections... wisheth for the fruit... covetous, endued with cruelty, and impure... passion. The agent who is void of application... obstinate, deceitful, malicious, slothful, desponding, and procrastinating, is said to be of the quality of darkness.' (Note: the Ganguli passage's 'action from delusion' line appears under 'passion' — likely a known textual slip; the dark-action description in the story follows the standard threefold teaching.)

statements.claim: Arjuna declared: 'My delusion hath been destroyed, and the recollection (of what I am) hath been gained by me... through thy favour. I am now firm. My doubts have been dispelled. I will do thy bidding.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, MBh 6.42: 'My delusion hath been destroyed, and the recollection (of what I am) hath been gained by me, O Undeteriorating one, through thy favour. I am now firm. My doubts have been dispelled. I will do thy bidding.'

statements.claim: The story frames Arjuna's resolution as the fruit of his having seen he was never sole author of his deeds and that fruit was never his to hoard.
statements.evidence: Interpretive summary of the chapter's five-causes and fruit-abandonment teaching — consistent with the source but phrased as reflection, not a new factual claim.

notes: Doctrine and dialogue match MBh 6.42 (BG ch. 18). One minor rendering note: the story assigns the 'action from delusion' (darkness) description correctly per the standard triad, whereas Ganguli's text as printed labels it 'passion' — the story follows the teaching's intent, so no correction needed. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: When Arjuna took up his arrows and Gandiva once more, the Pandava car-warriors raised a tremendous shout; the Pandavas and Somakas blew their sea-born conches, drums and cow-horns sounded, and the uproar was very loud.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43: 'Beholding Dhananjaya then to take up once again (his) arrows and Gandiva, the mighty car-warriors (of the Pandava party) uttered a tremendous shout. And those heroes, viz., the Pandavas and the Somakas... blew their sea-born conches. And drums, and Pesis, and Karkachas, and cow-horns were beaten and blown together, and the uproar made was very loud.'

statements.claim: The gods came with Gandharvas, Pitris, hosts of Siddhas and Charanas, and the blessed Rishis with Indra of the hundred sacrifices at their head, desiring to witness the great slaughter.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43: 'there came the gods, with Gandharvas and the Pitris, and the hosts of Siddhas and Charanas, from desire of witnessing (the sight). And Rishis highly blessed came there in a body with him (Indra) of a hundred sacrifices at their head, for beholding that great slaughter.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira the Just put off his coat of mail, cast aside his weapon, descended from his car and walked on foot with joined hands and restrained speech toward the hostile host, facing east, eyeing the grandsire; his brothers followed him, alarmed, and Arjuna, Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva called out asking where he was going without armor, leaving his brothers.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43: 'the heroic king Yudhishthira, the Just, putting off his coat of mail and casting aside his excellent weapon and quickly descending from his car, with joined hands, proceeded on foot, eyeing the grandsire, with restrained speech, facing the east, towards the direction where the hostile host was... Dhananjaya... followed him, accompanied by his (other) brothers... Arjuna said,--What is this act of thine, O king, that abandoning thy brothers, thou proceedest on foot... Bhimasena said,--Where wilt thou go, O king of kings, having cast off thy coat of mail and weapons... Nakula said... Sahadeva said...'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira said nothing and kept walking; Krishna, smiling, explained that his object was known to him — he had gone to pay his respects to his elders Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Shalya, for it is heard in the histories of old that he who honors preceptors, the revered in years and his kinsmen before battle is sure to obtain victory.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43: 'Yudhishthira of restrained speech said nothing but continued to proceed. Unto them (then), the high-souled Vasudeva... smilingly said,--His object is known to me. Having paid his respects to all his superiors (such as) Bhishma, Drona, and Kripa, and Salya also, he will fight the foe. It is heard in histories of olden times that he who, having paid his respects according to the ordinance unto his preceptors, revered in years and his kinsmen, fighteth... is sure to obtain victory in battle.'

statements.claim: The Kaurava ranks raised a loud uproar, jeering that Yudhishthira was an infamous wretch of his race come in terror to seek Bhishma's shelter, waved their garments, and censured Yudhishthira with his brothers and Kesava; Yudhishthira walked through it, penetrated the array bristling with arrows, and stood before the grandsire.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43: 'among the ranks of Dhritarashtra's son, a loud uproar of Alas, and Oh arose... This one is an infamous wretch of his race... this king is coming in terror towards Bhishma's side... all the warriors there (then) censured Yudhishthira with all his brothers and along with Kesava too... with cheerful hearts waved their garments... The king (meanwhile), penetrating the hostile array bristling with arrows and darts, proceeded quickly towards Bhishma.'

statements.claim: Seizing Bhishma's feet with both hands, Yudhishthira saluted the invincible one, said they would do battle with him, and asked his permission and blessing; Bhishma replied that had he not come thus he would have cursed him for bringing about his own defeat, that he was gratified, bidding him do battle and obtain victory and ask whatever boon he desired.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43: 'Seizing his feet with his two hands, the royal son of Pandu then said unto Santanu's son Bhishma... I salute thee, O invincible one. With thee we will do battle. Grant (us) thy permission in that matter. Give (us) also (thy) blessing.--Bhishma said,--If, O lord of the earth, thou hadst not... come to me thus, I would have... cursed thee... for bringing about thy defeat. I am gratified (with thee), O son. Do battle, and obtain victory... Solicit also the boon... which thou desirest to have from us.'

statements.claim: Krishna then went to Radha's son Karna on the field of battle and, for the sake of the Pandavas, said he had heard that out of hatred of Bhishma Karna would not fight, inviting him to come to the Pandavas' side and stay as long as Bhishma was not slain.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, MBh 6.43: 'Vasudeva then went to Radha's son on the field of battle. And the elder brother of Gada, for the sake of the Pandavas, then said to Karna,--It hath been heard by me, O Karna, that from hatred of Bhishma thou wilt not fight. Come to our side, O son of Radha, and (stay with us) as long as Bhishma is not slain.'

statements.claim: Karna refused without hesitation, saying he would not do anything disagreeable to Dhritarashtra's son — Duryodhana was his friend and his king and he would not be disloyal to him.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt, MBh 6.43: 'Karna said,--I will not do anything that is disagreeable to Dhritarashtra's son, O Kes[ava]...'; the loyalty-to-Duryodhana grounds for the refusal are the chapter's stated import (index summary: 'Karna refuses out of loyalty to Duryodhana') and the direct continuation of Karna's reply in the source.

statements.claim: Krishna's overture came right after Yudhishthira's courtesy visit to Bhishma, on the field before the armies met.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.43 sequence: the Karna episode follows Yudhishthira's exchange with Bhishma in the same chapter; pack excerpt places Krishna's approach 'on the field of battle.' (Variant note also cross-references the pre-war offer, mb_b_032.)

statements.claim: The offer was refused and the war would be fought with Karna on the side he had chosen; some loyalties are not bought.
statements.evidence: Closing reflection consistent with the sourced refusal; interpretive connective narration.

notes: Closely follows MBh 6.43 (Ganguli): Yudhishthira's walk to Bhishma, the jeers, the blessing, and Krishna's offer to Karna with Karna's refusal all match. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: When the troops withdrew on the first day, Duryodhana was filled with delight at Bhishma's wrathful prowess in battle, and Yudhishthira the Just came to Krishna with all his brothers and all the kings of his side, filled with great grief.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'When the troops... were withdrawn on the first day, and when Duryodhana was filled with delight upon (beholding) Bhishma excited with wrath in battle, king Yudhishthira the just, speedily repaired unto Janardana, accompanied by all his brothers and all the kings (on his side). Filled with great grief thinking of his defeat...'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira lamented that Bhishma consumed his troops with arrows like fire burning dry grass and licked up his army like fire fed with clarified butter; his soldiers flew away pierced and afflicted; enraged Yama, Indra armed with the thunderbolt, Varuna with his noose or Kuvera with his mace might be vanquished, but mighty Bhishma could not; he was sinking in the fathomless ocean of Bhishma without a boat.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'Behold, O Krishna, that mighty bowman Bhishma of terrible prowess. He consumes with his arrow my troops like fire (consuming) dry grass... licking up my troops like fire fed with clarified butter... my troops fly away, afflicted with arrows. Enraged Yama himself, or He armed with the thunder, or even Varuna noose in hand, or Kuvera armed with mace, may be vanquished in battle but the mighty car-warrior Bhishma, of great energy is incapable of being vanquished... I am sinking in the fathomless ocean represented by Bhishma, without a boat (to rescue me).'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira said that from the weakness of his understanding, having gotten Bhishma for a foe, he would retire into the woods — living there being preferable to devoting the lords of earth to Death in the form of Bhishma; his heroic brothers were pained and pierced with arrows for his sake, having given up sovereignty and happiness out of love for their eldest brother; during the remainder of his days he would practise the severest austerities and would not cause these friends to be slain.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'In consequence... of the weakness of my understanding, having obtained Bhishma (for a foe in battle), I shall, O Govinda, retire into woods. To live there is preferable to devoting these lords of earth to Death in the form of Bhishma... My heroic brothers also are pained and afflicted with arrows for my sake, having been deprived of both sovereignty and happiness in consequence of their love for their eldest brother... During the remainder of my days I will practise the severest of ascetic austerities. I will not, O Kesava, cause these friends of mine to be slain.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira complained that Arjuna was an indifferent spectator; only Bhima fought, remembering Kshatriya duty, achieving the most difficult feats with his hero-slaying mace among foot-soldiers, steeds, cars and elephants, yet could not destroy the hostile host in fair fight even in a century; Bhishma and Drona with their celestial weapons incessantly applied were consuming all the Kshatriyas.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'As regards Arjuna, I see that he is an indifferent spectator in this battle... this Bhima alone, remembering Kshatriya duties, fighteth... With his hero-slaying mace... achieveth the most difficult feats upon foot-soldiers and steeds and cars and elephants. This hero, however, is incapable... of destroying in fair fight the hostile host in even a century... The celestial weapons of Bhishma and the high-souled Drona, incessantly applied, are consuming all the Kshatriyas.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira asked Krishna to tell him without delay what should be done and to look for that great bowman, that mighty car-warrior, who would give Bhishma his quietus like rain-charged clouds quenching a forest conflagration, so that through Krishna's grace the Pandavas might recover their kingdom and be happy with their kinsmen.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'Tell me, O Madhava, without delay, what should be done that might do me good... look for that great bowman, that mighty car-warrior, who will give Bhishma his quietus like rain-charged clouds quenching a forest conflagration. (Then) through thy grace, O Govinda... the son of Pandu... will, after recovery of their kingdom, be happy with their kinsmen.'

statements.claim: The son of Pandu, heart afflicted, remained silent for a long while in a reflective mood with his mind turned inward.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'Having said this, the high-souled son of Pritha, with heart afflicted by grief and mind turned within, remained silent for a long while in a reflected mood.'

statements.claim: Krishna consoled him: he should not grieve when his brothers were all heroes and renowned bowmen; Krishna himself, Satyaki, Virata, Drupada, and Dhrishtadyumna of Prishata's line were employed in doing him good; the monarchs with their troops were devoted to him and expectant of his favour; his commander Dhrishtadyumna was always desirous of his welfare; and Sikhandin was certainly the slayer of Bhishma.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'Govinda then gladdening all the Pandavas said,--Do not grieve, O chief of the Bharatas. It behoveth thee not to grieve, when thy brothers are all heroes and renowned bowmen in the world. I also am employed in doing thee good, as also that mighty car-warrior Satyaki and Virata and Drupada... and Dhrishtadyumna of Prishata's line. And so also... all these monarchs with their (respective) troops are expectant of thy favour and devoted to thee... This mighty car-warrior Dhrishtadyumna... placed in command of thy army is always desirous of thy welfare and engaged in doing that which is agreeable to thee, as also this Sikhandin... who is certainly the slayer of Bhishma.'

statements.claim: In that very assembly, in the hearing of Vasudeva, Yudhishthira told Dhrishtadyumna to mark his words, that his words should not be transgressed, and that approved by Vasudeva he had been commander of the Pandava forces.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.50: 'Hearing these words, the king (Yudhishthira), said, unto that mighty car-warrior Dhrishtadyumna, in that very assembly and in the hearing of Vasudeva, these words,--O Dhrishtadyumna, mark these words that I say unto thee, O thou of Prishata's line. The words uttered by me should not be transgressed. Approved by Vasudeva, thou hast been the commander of our forces.'

statements.claim: Krishna's assurance that Sikhandin was Bhishma's destined slayer lifted Yudhishthira's despair and turned him back to giving orders for war.
statements.evidence: The narrative bridge between the sourced words ('This Sikhandin... is certainly the slayer of Bhishma') and Yudhishthira's immediate address to Dhrishtadyumna; the psychological framing is connective narration consistent with the source sequence.

notes: Lament, resolution-to-woods, complaint about Arjuna/Bhima, Krishna's consolation and the Sikhandin prophecy all track MBh 6.50 (Ganguli) closely. No unsupported or contradicted claims.
